title.narrative: Yaba Guy Che (For the men): Implementation and evaluation of a codeveloped multi-disease intervention for men to overcome health systems barriers

description.narrative: It is well-established that men in the Southern African region are less likely than women to access HIV/STI/TB and non-communicable disease (NCD) testing and treatment within traditional clinic-based services. This results in increased morbidity and mortality compared with women, and increased transmission of communicable diseases such as HIV, TB and STIs. Providing services that are responsive to men’s health needs has the potential to substantially increase men’s access to treatment and preventative health services. This research consortium will conduct interrelated research studies to demonstrate how health systems in urbanised areas can be strengthened to deliver comprehensive health services including for HIV/STI/TB and NCD for men. We will do this by implementing and evaluating a co-developed community-based delivery of services to men, in a large, high-density urban community in Lusaka, Zambia. Yaba Guy Che ( “For the guys”) was co-developed with men during 2022-2023 in a formative research study. The first step of the proposed consortium activities will be a workshop with policy makers, community members and district health facility staff to finalise the design of the intervention. Continuous community engagement through regular contact with the community members as well as through newly formed men’s peer groups will support the implementation of the Yaba Guy Che intervention. The key intervention will operationalise a digital health system, which will allow tracking of service use between community-based booths that provide services and are in “hotspots” where men congregate, complementary vending machines that provide commodities, and the primary health system for referrals. We will implement the Yaba Guy Che intervention for 24 months during which the response to the intervention will be monitored and reviewed. The plausible impact of the intervention in reaching men with services will be evaluated through a before and after study design which will measure the difference in coverage before and after implementation using time-location sampling surveys and estimate costs of implementation. We will convene a final workshop to share the results of the impact evaluation with community members and policy makers to critically discuss the results of the study. If successful, the discussion will include the scale-up of the model to other urban settings in the region and potential adaptations required to provide equitable access to services for men.

OBJECTIVES: 1. Co-develop an integrated, digitally supported care pathway (“Yaba Guy Che”) with men, community members, healthcare workers and policy-makers. 2. Deliver the Yaba Guy Che intervention and assess adoption, reach, fidelity, sustainability and scalability. 3. Create a men’s peer monitoring group to strengthen community health system accountability and document how men experience the Yaba Guy Che intervention. 4. Estimate the plausible impact of the Yaba Guy Che intervention on coverage of HIV and NCD services. 5. Measure the effect of the intervention across the six building blocks of the health system and assess the cost and economies of scope of implementing Yaba Guy Che to inform scalability and sustainability.
